definition_en: a person who controls how a film or play is made, or who leads a department or company
core_image: 片场中央一把折椅，椅背上印着名字，旁边的人都停下手等这个人发话
scene: 片场的灯全亮着，所有人放下手里的活，望向监视器后面那把椅子。The director asked for one more take.
sceneCN: 这里 director 指「导演」（第 1 个义项：影视或戏剧的总负责人）；句意是导演要求再拍一条。

senses.title: The one who shapes a film
senses.definition: a person who controls how a film, play or programme is made
senses.definitionCN: 掌管电影、戏剧或节目如何呈现的人
senses.example: The director cut the last scene from the film.
senses.exampleCN: 导演把最后一场戏从电影里剪掉了。
senses.why: Thirty people work, but one pair of eyes decides what stays.
senses.whyCN: 三十个人在干活，可留下什么只由一双眼睛决定。

senses.title: The head of a department
senses.definition: a senior person who manages a department or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 管理一个部门或机构的负责人
senses.example: She was promoted to director of the research centre.
senses.exampleCN: 她被提升为研究中心的主管。
senses.why: The door of an office carries a name, and that name answers for the room.
senses.whyCN: 办公室门上写着一个名字，这个名字就要为这间屋子负责。

senses.title: A seat on the board
senses.definition: one of the people chosen to guide the decisions of a company
senses.definitionCN: 被选来为公司决策把关的人
senses.example: The board of directors meets every Monday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会每周一上午开会。
senses.why: The company needs a group of names that can be blamed or trusted together.
senses.whyCN: 公司需要一组名字，能被一起问责，也能被一起信任。

intro.en: Director comes from Latin dirigere, to set straight or guide, and first named any person who guided or governed.
intro.cn: director 来自拉丁语 dirigere（拉直、指引），最初泛指引路或管事的人。

items.en: Dirigere meant to set a line straight or to guide a course.
items.cn: dirigere 指把一条线拉直，也指引导方向。

items.en: Directus, its past participle, described something laid straight.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 directus 形容被拉直的东西。

items.en: Director named a guide, a person who set others on a course.
items.cn: director 指引路者，把别人带上某条路的人。

items.en: English took the word for a governor or a head of an office.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，用来指管理者或机构首长。

items.en: The film industry gave it the everyday sense of the person behind the camera.
items.cn: 电影业又让它日常化，专指镜头背后的那个人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the direct- stem, while the meaning group names other people who lead a production or a team.
note.cn: 形近组共用 direct 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他带团队或带作品的人。

entries.definition: to guide a course or to aim something straight
entries.definitionCN: 指引方向或把某物对准

entries.definition: the line along which someone or something moves
entries.definitionCN: 人或物移动所沿的路线

entries.definition: an official instruction that tells people what to do
entries.definitionCN: 要求人们如何行事的正式指示

entries.definition: a person who makes films, especially one in charge of them
entries.definitionCN: 拍电影的人，尤指主导创作的人

entries.definition: a person who runs a team, a shop or a department
entries.definitionCN: 管理团队、店铺或部门的人

entries.definition: a person who watches over the work of others
entries.definitionCN: 监督他人工作的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks start at the chair with a name on it and end with the single word a whole set waits for.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一把印着名字的椅子开始，走到全组人都在等的那一句话。

normal.en: Direct plus -or is the one who gives the direction.
normal.cn: direct 加 -or，就是给方向的那个人。

normal.en: A film director says cut, and the scene stops.
normal.cn: 导演一喊停，整场戏就停住。

normal.en: A managing director runs the company, not the camera.
normal.cn: 总经理管公司，不管镜头。

normal.en: The board of directors sits above every department.
normal.cn: 董事会坐在所有部门之上。

normal.en: One name on the chair tells the whole crew who decides.
normal.cn: 椅子上印一个名字，全组就知道谁说了算。

abstract.en: Picture a folding chair with a name stencilled on the back.
abstract.cn: 想象一把折椅，椅背上印着名字。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised while thirty people freeze.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起，三十个人同时定住。

abstract.en: Picture one word travelling from that chair to every corner of the set.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话从那把椅子传到片场每个角落。

examples.en: The director asked the actor to say the line again.
examples.cn: 导演让演员把那句台词再说一遍。

examples.en: He became the director of a small research institute.
examples.cn: 他成了一家小研究所的主管。

examples.en: Two directors resigned after the bad year.
examples.cn: 糟糕的一年过后，两名董事辞职了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 director 记成「带路的」：direct 是给方向，-or 是人，替全组指方向的人就是导演。

root: 来自拉丁语 dirigere（把线拉直、指引），过去分词 directus 意为被引直的。director 在拉丁语里指引路者，进入英语后先指管事的人，后来才专指电影与戏剧的导演，也指部门主管与公司董事。

sensesIntro.en: From the person who calls the shots on a set, to the head of a department, to a seat on the company board.
sensesIntro.cn: 从片场里发号施令的人，到部门的主管，再到公司董事会里的一个席位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chair with a name on it, and a whole crew waiting for one word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把印着名字的椅子，一整组人都在等一句话。

branches.en: The first sense is the one who shapes a film or a play.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把电影或戏剧塑造成形的人。

branches.en: The second sense moves the same authority into an office.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把同一种权威搬进办公室。

branches.en: The third sense gives that authority a seat on a board.
branches.cn: 第三个义项给这种权威一个董事会的席位。

branches.en: Both senses share one act: choosing what the others will do.
branches.cn: 两个义项共有一个动作：决定别人该做什么。

branches.en: An office head and a board member both answer for a whole body.
branches.cn: 部门主管和董事都要为整个机构负责。

intro.en: Director gathers the direct- family, words about straight lines, guidance and command.
intro.cn: director 聚起 direct 一族词，围绕直线、指引与指挥。

latinIntro.en: Latin dirigere, to set straight, gives the stem direct-, seen in direct, direction and directive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dirigere（拉直）给出词干 direct，见于 direct、direction 与 directive。

items.example: The director chose a young actress for the part.
items.exampleCN: 导演选了一位年轻女演员演这个角色。

items.example: She directed the traffic around the hole.
items.exampleCN: 她指挥车辆绕过那个坑。

items.meaning: the line along which something moves
items.example: The wind changed direction at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 风在黄昏时换了方向。

items.example: A new directive reached every office.
items.exampleCN: 一道新指令下达到了每个办公室。

items.meaning: in a straight line or with nothing between
items.example: The train goes directly to the airport.
items.exampleCN: 这趟车直达机场。

items.meaning: not straight or not stated openly
items.example: He gave an indirect answer.
items.exampleCN: 他给了一个间接的回答。

items.meaning: the group of directors of a company
items.example: The directorate approved the budget.
items.exampleCN: 董事会批准了预算。

items.meaning: to send or aim something wrongly
items.example: The sign misdirected half the visitors.
items.exampleCN: 那块牌子把一半游客指错了路。

definition_en: a list of names, addresses or files arranged so that a particular item can be found
core_image: 前台抽屉里一本厚册子，一列列名字和号码排得像梯子
scene: 册子摊在台面上，纸边被翻得起了毛。He found the number in the telephone directory.
sceneCN: 这里 directory 指「名录」（第 1 个义项：按顺序排列的名单册）；句意是他在电话簿里查到了那个号码。

senses.title: A book of names and numbers
senses.definition: a book or list that gives names, addresses or telephone numbers in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序列出姓名、地址或电话的册子或清单
senses.example: He found the number in the telephone directory.
senses.exampleCN: 他在电话簿里查到了那个号码。
senses.why: A town full of strangers becomes findable once the names are set in rows.
senses.whyCN: 一城陌生人，只要名字排成行，就变得可以找到了。

senses.title: An index of stored items
senses.definition: a list that shows where things are kept or how they are arranged
senses.definitionCN: 标明东西存放位置或排列方式的清单
senses.example: The directory at the back of the report lists every table.
senses.exampleCN: 报告末尾的目录列出了每一张表。
senses.why: The list does not hold the thing, only the way to reach it.
senses.whyCN: 这份清单不装着东西，只装着找到东西的路。

senses.title: A folder on a computer
senses.definition: a named area on a computer that holds files and other folders
senses.definitionCN: 电脑里存放文件与其他文件夹的有名空间
senses.example: Save the pictures in a separate directory.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些图片存到另一个文件夹里。
senses.why: The paper list became a room, and the room can hold rooms inside it.
senses.whyCN: 纸上的清单变成了一间屋子，而屋子还能再装屋子。

intro.en: Directory began as a medieval Latin directorium, a guide or book of rules, and only later became a list of names.
intro.cn: directory 原是中世纪拉丁语 directorium，指指南或规则手册，后来才变成名单。

items.en: Dirigere meant to set straight and to guide a course.
items.cn: dirigere 指拉直，也指引导方向。

items.en: Directorium named a guide or a book that told people what to do.
items.cn: directorium 指指南，或告诉人该怎么做的书。

items.en: English directory first meant a set of directions or rules.
items.cn: 英语里的 directory 最初指一套指示或规则。

items.en: The word shifted to a book of names, addresses and numbers.
items.cn: 这个词转而指收录姓名、地址与号码的册子。

items.en: Computing added the sense of a folder that lists files.
items.cn: 计算机又给它添了「列出文件的文件夹」这一义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the direct- stem, while the meaning group names other ordered lists.
note.cn: 形近组共用 direct 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他有序的清单。

entries.definition: to guide a course or to aim something straight
entries.definitionCN: 指引方向或把某物对准

entries.definition: the line along which someone or something moves
entries.definitionCN: 人或物移动所沿的路线

entries.definition: a person who controls how a film is made
entries.definitionCN: 掌管电影拍摄的人

entries.definition: an ordered list that points to where information is found
entries.definitionCN: 指向信息所在位置的有序清单

entries.definition: a list of goods or items arranged for reference
entries.definitionCN: 供查阅而编排的货品或条目清单

entries.definition: a published list of names, events or properties
entries.definitionCN: 公布出来的名单、活动或房产清单

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a thick book of names to a folder that holds other folders.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一本厚厚的名单册，走到能装下其他文件夹的文件夹。

normal.en: Direct plus -ory is a place where things are set in order.
normal.cn: direct 加 -ory，就是把东西排整齐的地方。

normal.en: A telephone directory turns a city into rows of names.
normal.cn: 电话簿把一座城变成一排排名字。

normal.en: A directory never holds the thing, only its address.
normal.cn: 名录从不装着东西，只装着它的地址。

normal.en: On a computer, a directory is a folder with a name.
normal.cn: 在电脑里，directory 就是有名字的文件夹。

normal.en: Look up the name, then follow the number.
normal.cn: 先查名字，再顺着号码找过去。

abstract.en: Picture a finger sliding down a column of names.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿着一列名字往下滑。

abstract.en: Picture a page thin enough to show the print from behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一页薄纸，背面的字都透了过来。

abstract.en: Picture a folder opening to show smaller folders inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件夹打开，里面还有更小的文件夹。

examples.en: The library keeps a directory of local clubs.
examples.cn: 图书馆存着一份本地社团名录。

examples.en: She searched the directory for his office number.
examples.cn: 她在名录里查他办公室的号码。

examples.en: Copy the file into the main directory.
examples.cn: 把这个文件复制到主文件夹里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 directory 记成「的名字全录」：direct 是排直，-ory 是地方，把名字排直放好的地方就是名录。

root: 来自拉丁语 dirigere（拉直、指引）的名词形式 directorium，本指指南或规则手册。英语先用它表示指示与规则，十八世纪后转向姓名地址录，计算机时代又用来指存放文件的文件夹。

sensesIntro.en: From a printed book of names, to an index of stored things, to a folder on a screen.
sensesIntro.cn: 从印着名字的册子，到存放物品的索引，再到屏幕上的文件夹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick book of names set in straight rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本厚册子，名字排成笔直的行。

chain: THE NAMES ARE COPIED IN ORDER
A COMPUTER KEEPS ITS OWN LIST
FILES SIT INSIDE A NAMED SPACE

branches.en: The first sense is the printed book of names and numbers.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那本印着姓名与号码的册子。

branches.en: The second sense narrows the book to a guide of places.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这本书收窄成指路的清单。

branches.en: The third sense gives the list a room inside a machine.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这份清单搬进机器里的一间屋子。

branches.en: A book and an index both answer one question: where is it.
branches.cn: 册子和索引都在回答同一个问题：它在哪儿。

branches.en: Both arrange hidden things so that one search finds them.
branches.cn: 两者都把藏着的东西排好，让一次查找就能找到。

intro.en: Directory belongs to the direct- family, words about straight lines and guidance.
intro.cn: directory 属于 direct 一族词，围绕直线与指引。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base dirigere, to set straight, yields direct-, seen in direct, direction and directory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 dirigere（拉直）给出 direct，见于 direct、direction 与 directory。

items.meaning: a place or book that keeps things in order
items.example: The directory lists every member of the club.
items.exampleCN: 这份名录列出了俱乐部的每位成员。

items.example: He directed us to the nearest station.
items.exampleCN: 他给我们指了最近的车站。

items.meaning: the line along which something moves
items.example: She walked in the direction of the river.
items.exampleCN: 她朝河的方向走去。

items.example: The director smiled at the finished scene.
items.exampleCN: 导演看着拍完的这场戏笑了。

items.example: The directive was short and firm.
items.exampleCN: 那道指令简短而强硬。

items.meaning: in a straight line or with nothing between
items.example: The road runs directly to the coast.
items.exampleCN: 这条路直通海岸。

items.meaning: not straight or not stated openly
items.example: Her reply was polite but indirect.
items.exampleCN: 她的回答客气却绕弯。

items.meaning: to send or aim something wrongly
items.example: A wrong label misdirected the parcel.
items.exampleCN: 一个错误的标签把包裹送错了地方。

definition_en: loose earth, dust or unwanted matter that makes something unclean
core_image: 指甲缝里嵌着一圈黑泥，用水冲也冲不干净
scene: 孩子从院子里跑进来，鞋底在地板上留下一串土印。He washed the dirt off his hands.
sceneCN: 这里 dirt 指「污垢」（第 1 个义项：沾在东西上的脏物）；句意是他把手上的泥洗掉了。

senses.title: Matter that makes things unclean
senses.definition: dust, mud or grease that spoils the surface it touches
senses.definitionCN: 落在表面上、把东西弄脏的灰、泥或油污
senses.example: He washed the dirt off his hands.
senses.exampleCN: 他把手上的泥洗掉了。
senses.why: You can see where it has been, even after it is gone.
senses.whyCN: 就算它被洗掉了，你仍看得出它待过哪里。

senses.title: Loose earth on the ground
senses.definition: the soft brown material that covers the ground
senses.definitionCN: 铺在地面上的松软褐色物质
senses.example: The children played in the dirt behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在屋后的泥地里玩。
senses.why: The same word names the ground itself and the mark it leaves.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指地面本身，也指它留下的印子。

senses.title: Hidden scandal about a person
senses.definition: unpleasant private information that can harm someone's name
senses.definitionCN: 能损害某人名声的难堪私事
senses.example: The paper paid a lot for dirt on the mayor.
senses.exampleCN: 那家报纸花了不少钱买市长的把柄。
senses.why: A stain on a name works like a stain on cloth.
senses.whyCN: 名字上的污点，和布上的污点一样难洗。

intro.en: Dirt came from Old Norse drit, a word for filth, and pushed aside the older English terms for mud and waste.
intro.cn: dirt 来自古诺斯语 drit（污秽），挤掉了英语原有的几个说法。

items.en: A root drit- named filth and waste matter.
items.cn: 词根 drit- 指污秽与排泄物。

items.en: Drit meant excrement or any filthy substance.
items.cn: drit 指排泄物或任何污秽之物。

items.en: Drit and dirt named mud, dung and waste on the ground.
items.cn: drit 与 dirt 指地上的泥、粪与脏东西。

items.en: Dirt widened to include loose earth as well as filth.
items.cn: dirt 的用法扩大，既指污秽也指松散的泥土。

items.en: The word now covers dust, mud and hidden scandal alike.
items.cn: 如今这个词兼指灰尘、泥土与见不得光的丑事。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a single sound, while the meaning group names kinds of earth and waste.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音，近义组则区分几种土与脏物。

entries.definition: to move quickly and suddenly
entries.definitionCN: 飞快地突然移动

entries.definition: force or effort, used in the phrase by dint of
entries.definitionCN: 力量或努力，见于 by dint of 一语

entries.definition: a long dagger once carried in Scotland
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰人从前佩带的长匕首

entries.definition: the upper layer of earth in which plants grow
entries.definitionCN: 植物生长的表层土壤

entries.definition: wet earth that sticks to shoes and clothes
entries.definitionCN: 粘在鞋和衣服上的湿泥

entries.definition: fine dry powder that settles on surfaces
entries.definitionCN: 落在表面的细干粉末

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from mud on a shoe to a stain that cannot be washed off a name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从鞋上的泥，走到名字上洗不掉的污点。

normal.en: Dirt is short and ugly, like the mark it leaves.
normal.cn: dirt 这个词又短又硬，像它留下的那道印子。

normal.en: Dirt makes a clean thing show where it has been.
normal.cn: 干净的东西一沾上污垢，就显出它待过哪里。

normal.en: A dirt road is named for what it is made of.
normal.cn: 土路就是以它所用的材料命名的。

normal.en: Dirt cheap means the price is as low as the ground.
normal.cn: dirt cheap 是说价钱低到贴着地面。

normal.en: Dirt on a person is a stain that water cannot reach.
normal.cn: 一个人身上的 dirt，是一盆水洗不到的污点。

abstract.en: Picture a thumb pressed into soft brown earth.
abstract.cn: 想象一根拇指按进松软的褐色泥土。

abstract.en: Picture a white cloth with one dark fingerprint.
abstract.cn: 想象一块白布上有一个深色指印。

abstract.en: Picture a page of gossip folded small and hidden.
abstract.cn: 想象一页闲话被折小、藏了起来。

examples.en: There was dirt under every fingernail.
examples.cn: 每片指甲底下都是泥。

examples.en: The bike threw dirt onto the clean floor.
examples.cn: 自行车把泥甩到了干净的地板上。

examples.en: They built the hut on a dirt floor.
examples.cn: 他们把棚屋盖在泥地上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dirt 记成「得特脏」：这东西一沾身，就得特意去洗一遍。

root: 来自古诺斯语 drit，指污秽与排泄物，与古英语中几个表示泥污的词竞争后胜出。十六世纪起，词义从污秽扩展到松散的泥土；后来又引申为一个人见不得光的丑事，像名字上的一块污迹。

sensesIntro.en: From the mark on a hand, to the earth under a hut, to the scandal that stains a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 从手上的泥印，到棚屋下的泥地，再到玷污名声的丑事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark mark left where a clean surface was touched.
core.cn: 核心意象：干净表面被碰过之后留下的深色印子。

branches.cn: 第一个义项是弄脏表面的污物。

branches.en: The second sense is the earth itself, loose underfoot.
branches.cn: 第二个义项就是脚下的松土。

branches.en: The third sense turns the stain into a hidden story.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把污迹变成一段藏起来的往事。

branches.en: The ground and the mark it leaves share one name.
branches.cn: 泥土与它留下的印子共用一个名字。

branches.en: Both kinds of dirt are hard to remove once seen.
branches.cn: 两种 dirt 一旦被看见，都很难洗掉。

intro.en: Dirt is a short base that builds a small family of adjectives, adverbs and compounds.
intro.cn: dirt 是个短词基，带出一小族形容词、副词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the word came from Old Norse and grows with English endings.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根；这个词出自古诺斯语，靠英语词尾生长。

items.example: The dirt came off with warm water.
items.exampleCN: 污垢用温水就洗掉了。

items.example: His shoes were dirty after the walk.
items.exampleCN: 走完那段路他的鞋脏了。

items.example: The dirtiness of the room shocked her.
items.exampleCN: 房间的肮脏让她吃惊。

items.example: The windows were dirtily smeared.
items.exampleCN: 窗子被抹得脏兮兮的。

items.example: Only a dirtbag would cheat a child.
items.exampleCN: 只有无赖才会骗小孩。

items.meaning: a light motorcycle made for rough ground
items.example: He rode a dirt bike along the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 他骑着越野摩托沿山脊走。

items.meaning: a road made of packed earth
items.example: The dirt road turned to mud in the rain.
items.exampleCN: 一下雨土路就变成了泥。

items.example: The old chairs were dirt cheap.
items.exampleCN: 那些旧椅子便宜得离谱。

definition_en: covered with dirt, unfair or mean, or to make something unclean
core_image: 白球鞋踩进泥坑，抬起来时鞋面糊了一片褐色
scene: 球鞋在门口蹭了两下，还是在地垫上留下泥印。He came home with dirty hands.
sceneCN: 这里 dirty 指「脏的」（第 1 个义项：沾满污物的）；句意是他回家时两手都是泥。

senses.title: Covered with dirt
senses.definition: not clean, with dust, mud or grease on the surface
senses.definitionCN: 不干净，表面沾着灰、泥或油
senses.example: Put the dirty clothes in the basket.
senses.exampleCN: 把脏衣服放进篮子里。
senses.why: The surface shows every touch it has taken.
senses.whyCN: 表面把它受过的每一次触碰都显了出来。

senses.title: Mean and unfair
senses.definition: done in a dishonest or cruel way to harm someone
senses.definitionCN: 用不诚实或残忍的方式伤害别人
senses.example: That was a dirty trick to play on a friend.
senses.exampleCN: 那样算计朋友，手段太卑劣了。
senses.why: The act leaves a stain on the one who does it.
senses.whyCN: 这种举动会在做的人身上留下污点。

senses.title: To make something unclean
senses.definition: to put dirt on something or make it dirty
senses.definitionCN: 把污物弄到某物上，使它变脏
senses.example: He dirtied his new shirt at lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 他午饭时把新衬衫弄脏了。
senses.why: The adjective turns into an act the moment a hand does it.
senses.whyCN: 手一碰，形容词就变成了一个动作。

intro.en: Dirty is simply dirt with the adjective ending -y, first recorded in Middle English.
intro.cn: dirty 就是 dirt 加上形容词词尾 -y，最早见于中古英语。

items.en: Drit named filth and waste matter.
items.cn: drit 指污秽与脏物。

items.en: Dritty described something covered with filth.
items.cn: dritty 形容沾满污物的东西。

items.en: The spelling settled as dirty.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 dirty。

items.en: The word gained the sense of unfair or mean conduct.
items.cn: 这个词又添了「不公平、卑劣」的意思。

items.en: It works as an adjective and as a verb meaning to make unclean.
items.cn: 它既是形容词，也作动词表示弄脏。

note.en: The look-alike group is close in sound but far in meaning, while the meaning group offers stronger words for the same idea.
note.cn: 形近组读音相近、意思却远，近义组则给出同一意思的更强说法。

entries.definition: a place where milk is kept and butter is made
entries.definitionCN: 存放牛奶、制作黄油的场所

entries.definition: a book in which a person writes each day
entries.definitionCN: 按日记录的书册

entries.definition: something a person must do or owes to others
entries.definitionCN: 必须做或应尽的事

entries.definition: extremely dirty and unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 极其肮脏难忍的

entries.definition: covered with wet earth
entries.definitionCN: 沾满湿泥的

entries.definition: made dirty, especially cloth or paper
entries.definitionCN: 被弄脏的，尤指布或纸

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a muddy shoe to the kind of act that stains a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只沾泥的鞋，走到那种在人身上留下污点的行为。

normal.en: Dirty is dirt plus y: the adjective of the stain.
normal.cn: dirty 就是 dirt 加 y，是污迹的形容词。

normal.en: A dirty trick leaves no mud, but the mark lasts longer.
normal.cn: 卑鄙手段不沾泥，可留下的印子更久。

normal.en: Dirty laundry means both the clothes and the family secrets.
normal.cn: dirty laundry 既指脏衣服，也指家丑。

normal.en: To dirty a shirt is to make the adjective happen.
normal.cn: 把衬衫弄脏，就是让这个形容词发生。

normal.en: The dirtiest hands are often the ones that did the work.
normal.cn: 最脏的手，往往才是真正干过活的手。

abstract.en: Picture one brown print on a white shoe.
abstract.cn: 想象白鞋上有一个褐色脚印。

abstract.en: Picture water turning grey as it leaves a cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象水从布上流过时变成灰色。

abstract.en: Picture a whisper that makes a clean name look stained.
abstract.cn: 想象一句悄悄话，让干净的名声看着像有了污点。

examples.en: The dirty dishes were piled beside the sink.
examples.cn: 脏盘子堆在水池边。

examples.en: He dirtied his shoes in the wet field.
examples.cn: 他在湿地里弄脏了鞋。

examples.en: It was a dirty way to win the game.
examples.cn: 用那种方式赢下比赛，实在卑劣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dirty 记成「得特衣」：衣服一得特地去洗，就是脏了。

root: 由古诺斯语 drit（污秽）加上形容词词尾 -y 构成，中古英语写作 dritty。它先只表示沾满污物，十九世纪起又用来形容不公平、卑劣的行为，并进一步作动词，表示把东西弄脏。

sensesIntro.en: From a surface covered with mud, to an act that harms a friend, to the verb that puts the stain there.
sensesIntro.cn: 从沾满泥的表面，到伤害朋友的行为，再到把污迹弄上去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean white surface with one brown mark on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：干净的白色表面，上面落了一个褐色印子。

chain: A MEAN ACT LEAVES THE SAME STAIN
THE VERB PUTS THE STAIN THERE

branches.en: The first sense is the plain state of being unclean.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是不干净这个状态本身。

branches.en: The second sense moves the stain from cloth to conduct.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把污迹从布上移到行为上。

branches.en: The third sense is the act that makes the adjective true.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是让这个形容词成立的动作。

branches.en: Something is dirty only because someone dirtied it.
branches.cn: 东西之所以脏，是因为有人把它弄脏了。

branches.en: A stained shirt and a stained name are both hard to clean.
branches.cn: 脏衬衫和坏名声都一样难洗干净。

intro.en: Dirty sits at the centre of a small family built on the base dirt.
intro.cn: dirty 处在以 dirt 为词基的一小族词中央。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic, not Latin, and the family grows with English endings.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词基来自日耳曼语而非拉丁语，靠英语词尾生长。

items.example: The floor was dirty after the rain.
items.exampleCN: 下雨后地板很脏。

items.example: Dirt filled the cracks in the wall.
items.exampleCN: 泥土填满了墙上的裂缝。

items.example: He could not bear the dirtiness of the kitchen.
items.exampleCN: 他受不了厨房那股脏。

items.example: The cups were dirtily stacked.
items.exampleCN: 杯子脏兮兮地摞在一起。

items.example: His coat grew dirtier each day.
items.exampleCN: 他的外套一天比一天脏。

items.example: This is the dirtiest corner of the yard.
items.exampleCN: 这是院子里最脏的角落。

items.meaning: the act of making something unclean
items.example: He was dirtying every towel in the house.
items.exampleCN: 他把家里的毛巾一条条弄脏。

items.example: The rain dirtied the clean windows.
items.exampleCN: 雨把干净的窗子弄脏了。

definition_en: to stop a device or system from working, or to make someone unable to use part of the body
core_image: 一只手按下开关，屏幕上的一排按钮同时变成灰色
scene: 他蹲在机箱后面，把那根细线从接口里拔了出来。A single broken wire can disable the whole alarm.
sceneCN: 这里 disable 指「使失效」（第 1 个义项：让设备无法工作）；句意是一根断线就能让整套警报失灵。

senses.title: To put a machine out of action
senses.definition: to damage or switch off a device so that it cannot work
senses.definitionCN: 损坏或关掉设备，使它无法运转
senses.example: The storm disabled the power lines.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴让电线断了电。
senses.why: One small part stops, and everything that depended on it stops too.
senses.whyCN: 一个小零件停了，靠它运转的一切也跟着停。

senses.title: To take away bodily power
senses.definition: to make a person unable to move or use part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 使人无法活动或使用身体的某一部分
senses.example: A fall disabled him for several months.
senses.exampleCN: 一次摔倒让他几个月不能行动。
senses.why: The body is still there, but one road inside it is closed.
senses.whyCN: 身体还在，只是里面有一条路被封住了。

senses.title: To switch off a feature
senses.definition: to turn off an option or an account in a system
senses.definitionCN: 在系统里关掉某个选项或账号
senses.example: You can disable the camera in the settings.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以在设置里关掉相机。
senses.why: Nothing is broken; someone simply decides it will not answer.
senses.whyCN: 什么都没坏，只是有人决定让它不再回应。

intro.en: Disable joins the negative prefix dis- to able, and first meant to make someone unable in law.
intro.cn: disable 由否定前缀 dis- 加 able 构成，最初指使人在法律上失去资格。

items.en: Habilis meant easy to handle or fit for use.
items.cn: habilis 指好使唤的、合用的。

items.en: The prefix dis- reversed the quality, giving the sense of not able.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 把这一性质反过来，给出「不能」的意思。

items.en: To disable first meant to make a person legally unable.
items.cn: disable 最初指使某人在法律上失去资格。

items.en: The word spread from people to machines and their parts.
items.cn: 这个词从人扩展到机器及其零件。

items.en: It now also means to switch off a software feature.
items.cn: 如今它也指关闭软件中的某项功能。

note.en: The look-alike group plays with able and its negation, while the meaning group names ways of stopping something.
note.cn: 形近组在 able 及其否定形式上做文章，近义组则列出几种让东西停下的说法。

entries.definition: to make someone or something able to do something
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物能够做某事

entries.definition: not having the power or chance to do something
entries.definitionCN: 没有能力或机会做某事

entries.definition: in a skilful and competent way
entries.definitionCN: 能干地；巧妙地

entries.definition: to make a device or system stop working
entries.definitionCN: 使设备或系统停止工作

entries.definition: to damage something so badly that it cannot work
entries.definitionCN: 严重损坏某物使其无法运作

entries.definition: to weaken a power or a function
entries.definitionCN: 削弱某种能力或功能

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a switch that will not move to a body that will not answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从按不动的开关，走到不再回应的身体。

normal.en: Dis- means not, so disable means not able.
normal.cn: dis- 是「不」，disable 就是「不能」。

normal.en: One grey button can turn a whole machine off.
normal.cn: 一个变灰的按钮，就能让整台机器停下。

normal.en: A disabled account cannot log in.
normal.cn: 被停用的账号登不进去。

normal.en: A broken wire disables more than itself.
normal.cn: 一根断线停下的不只是它自己。

normal.en: The word takes away ability, not the thing itself.
normal.cn: 这个词拿走的是能力，不是东西本身。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling one small plug.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手拔掉一个小小的插头。

abstract.en: Picture a long row of lights going dark from left to right.
abstract.cn: 想象一排灯从左到右依次暗下去。

abstract.en: Picture a door that still stands but no longer opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门还在，却再也打不开。

examples.en: The storm disabled the power lines.
examples.cn: 风暴让电线断了电。

examples.en: A fall disabled him for several months.
examples.cn: 一次摔倒让他几个月不能行动。

examples.en: You can disable the camera in the settings.
examples.cn: 你可以在设置里关掉相机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disable 记成「敌塞包」：敌人往机器里塞了个包，机器就失效了。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 able（能够）构成，字面就是「使不能」。十五世纪先指使人在法律上失去资格，后来泛指使人失去行动能力，现代又用于设备、账号与软件功能的失效。

sensesIntro.en: From a machine that stops, to a body that cannot answer, to a feature switched off in a menu.
sensesIntro.cn: 从停下的机器，到不听使唤的身体，再到菜单里被关掉的功能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small plug pulled out, and everything behind it goes dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小小的插头被拔掉，后面的一切都暗了。

branches.en: The first sense is a device that can no longer work.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是再也无法工作的设备。

branches.en: The second sense is a body that can no longer move freely.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是再也无法自由活动的身体。

branches.en: The third sense is a feature that has been switched off.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是被关掉的一项功能。

branches.en: A dead machine and a grey button both lose their power to answer.
branches.cn: 停下的机器和变灰的按钮，都失去了回应的能力。

branches.en: In both cases the frame remains and the power is gone.
branches.cn: 两种情形里，架子都还在，力气却没了。

intro.en: Disable gathers the able family, words about power, skill and its loss.
intro.cn: disable 聚起 able 一族词，围绕能力、本领与失去。

latinIntro.en: Latin habilis, fit for use, gives able; the prefix dis- turns that fitness into its opposite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habilis（合用）给出 able，前缀 dis- 又把这份能力翻转过来。

items.example: The crash disabled the control system.
items.exampleCN: 那次撞车让控制系统失灵了。

items.meaning: having the power or skill to do something
items.example: She was able to finish the work alone.
items.exampleCN: 她一个人就能干完这活。

items.meaning: the power or skill to do something
items.example: He has a natural ability for music.
items.exampleCN: 他有音乐天赋。

items.meaning: to make someone able to do something
items.example: This card enables you to enter the lab.
items.exampleCN: 这张卡让你能进实验室。

items.example: He was unable to answer the question.
items.exampleCN: 他答不上那个问题。

items.meaning: having a condition that limits movement
items.example: The lift serves disabled visitors.
items.exampleCN: 这部电梯供行动不便的访客使用。

items.meaning: a condition that limits a person's ability
items.example: The ramp helps people with a disability.
items.exampleCN: 这道坡道方便有残疾的人。

items.meaning: the state of being made unable
items.example: The accident led to a long disablement.
items.exampleCN: 那场事故导致他长期丧失劳动能力。

definition_en: something that makes a person or plan less likely to succeed
core_image: 起跑线上，一只脚被沙袋压住，别人已经冲出去
scene: 等候的人看了看墙上的钟，又低头看自己磨破的鞋尖。The main disadvantage of the plan is its cost.
sceneCN: 这里 disadvantage 指「缺点」（第 1 个义项：不利之处）；句意是这个方案的主要缺点是成本。

senses.title: A condition that holds you back
senses.definition: something that makes success harder for a person or a plan
senses.definitionCN: 使个人或计划更难成功的因素
senses.example: The main disadvantage of the plan is its cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案的主要缺点是成本。
senses.why: Every choice closes a door as well as opening one.
senses.whyCN: 每个选择在开一扇门时，也关上了一扇。

senses.title: A weaker position in a contest
senses.definition: a position in which someone has less power or fewer chances than others
senses.definitionCN: 权力或机会不如别人的处境
senses.example: Small shops work at a disadvantage against big chains.
senses.exampleCN: 小店面对大型连锁处于劣势。
senses.why: The race is the same length, but one runner starts further back.
senses.whyCN: 赛程一样长，可有一个选手从更后面起步。

senses.title: Harm or loss to someone
senses.definition: harm or loss that comes to a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 落到个人或群体身上的损害或损失
senses.example: The new rule works to the disadvantage of young workers.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定对年轻工人不利。
senses.why: What blocks one person's road can also empty another's pocket.
senses.whyCN: 挡住一个人的路，也可能掏空另一个人的口袋。

intro.en: Disadvantage came from Old French desavantage, built on avant, before, with a negative prefix attached.
intro.cn: disadvantage 来自古法语 desavantage，词基是 avant（在前），前面加了否定成分。

items.en: Abante meant from before, and gave Old French avant.
items.cn: abante 指从前面起，后来变成古法语 avant。

items.en: Avantage named a position ahead of others.
items.cn: avantage 指走在别人前面的有利位置。

items.en: Desavantage reversed that position into a weaker one.
items.cn: desavantage 把这个位置反转成较弱的处境。

items.en: English borrowed the word as disadvantage.
items.cn: 英语把这个词借了进来，写作 disadvantage。

items.en: It now covers costs, weak positions and actual harm.
items.cn: 如今它兼指代价、劣势与实际损害。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the advantage stem, while the meaning group names other things that hold a person back.
note.cn: 形近组共用 advantage 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他拖住人的因素。

entries.definition: something that helps a person or plan succeed
entries.definitionCN: 有助于人或计划成功的因素

entries.definition: having fewer chances or resources than others
entries.definitionCN: 机会或资源少于他人的

entries.definition: likely to bring success or benefit
entries.definitionCN: 很可能带来成功或好处的

entries.definition: a fact that makes something less useful or attractive
entries.definitionCN: 使某物用处或吸引力降低的因素

entries.definition: a condition that makes success harder
entries.definitionCN: 使成功更困难的条件

entries.definition: the negative side of a choice or situation
entries.definitionCN: 选择或局面的负面一面

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a weight on one foot to the hidden cost inside a good plan.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从压在一只脚上的沙袋，走到好方案里藏着的代价。

normal.en: Dis- plus advantage is simply the advantage turned around.
normal.cn: dis- 加 advantage，就是把优势翻了个面。

normal.en: At a disadvantage means the race starts a step behind.
normal.cn: at a disadvantage 是说起跑时慢了半步。

normal.en: Every cheap plan hides a disadvantage in its price.
normal.cn: 每个便宜方案都把缺点藏进了价钱里。

normal.en: A disadvantage is a door that only opens inward.
normal.cn: 缺点是一扇只能往里开的门。

normal.en: List the disadvantages first, and the choice becomes clear.
normal.cn: 先把缺点列出来，选择就清楚了。

abstract.en: Picture a sandbag tied to one running shoe.
abstract.cn: 想象一只跑鞋上系着沙袋。

abstract.en: Picture a map with one road crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上有一条路被划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag with a second small number underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象价签下面还印着一个更小的数字。

examples.en: The plan has one clear disadvantage.
examples.cn: 这个方案有一个明显的缺点。

examples.en: Small shops work at a disadvantage against big chains.
examples.cn: 小店面对大型连锁处于劣势。

examples.en: They discussed the advantages and disadvantages of moving.
examples.cn: 他们讨论了搬家的利与弊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disadvantage 记成「定死得晚」：机会定死了还来得晚，自然就是不利条件。

root: 来自古法语 desavantage，词基 avant 出自拉丁语 abante（在前），本指「前面的位置」。加否定成分后表示「不在前头」，于是引申为缺点、劣势与由此带来的损害。

sensesIntro.en: From a flaw inside a plan, to a weaker starting position, to real harm that follows.
sensesIntro.cn: 从方案里的一个缺陷，到更弱的起跑位置，再到随后而来的实际损害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one runner starts with a weight tied to a foot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个选手起跑时脚上绑着重量。

chain: EVERY RACE HAS A STARTING LINE
A PLAN CARRIES ITS OWN WEIGHT

branches.en: The first sense is the flaw that slows a plan.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是拖慢方案的那个缺陷。

branches.en: The second sense is the weaker place on the starting line.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是起跑线上更弱的位置。

branches.en: The third sense is the loss that reaches a real person.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是落到真人身上的损失。

branches.en: A flaw and a weak position both shorten a person's chances.
branches.cn: 缺陷与劣势都会缩短一个人的机会。

branches.en: Whoever starts behind is the first to feel the harm.
branches.cn: 起步在后的人，总是最先尝到损害。

intro.en: Disadvantage belongs to the advantage family, all built on the idea of being in front.
intro.cn: disadvantage 属于 advantage 一族，核心都是「在前」。

latinIntro.en: Latin abante, from before, became Old French avant, the base of advantage and disadvantage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abante（从前面）变成古法语 avant，是 advantage 与 disadvantage 的词基。

items.meaning: a condition that holds a person back
items.example: The disadvantage of the plan is its cost.
items.exampleCN: 这个方案的缺点是成本。

items.example: Speed is her greatest advantage.
items.exampleCN: 速度是她最大的优势。

items.example: They chose an advantageous place to meet.
items.exampleCN: 他们选了一个有利的会面地点。

items.meaning: likely to bring loss or trouble
items.example: The deal was disadvantageous to the buyer.
items.exampleCN: 这笔交易对买方不利。

items.example: The school helps disadvantaged children.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校帮助处境不利的孩子。

items.meaning: in a way that brings benefit
items.example: The house was advantageously placed near the road.
items.exampleCN: 那房子位置有利，靠近大路。

items.example: The army advanced before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 军队在黎明前推进。

items.example: She joined an advanced class.
items.exampleCN: 她进了一个高级班。

definition_en: to have a different opinion, or to fail to match or suit something
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子，一个摇头，一个把杯子往前一推
scene: 会议桌上摊着两份预算，谁也没有去碰对方那张纸。She disagreed with every point in the report.
sceneCN: 这里 disagreed 指「不同意」（第 1 个义项：意见不同）；句意是报告里的每一点她都不同意。

senses.title: To hold a different opinion
senses.definition: to think that another person's view is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 认为别人的看法不对
senses.example: She disagreed with every point in the report.
senses.exampleCN: 报告里的每一点她都不同意。
senses.why: Two people can look at one page and see two different worlds.
senses.whyCN: 两个人看同一页纸，却看见两个不同的世界。

senses.title: To fail to match
senses.definition: to be different from something that should be the same
senses.definitionCN: 与本应相同的东西对不上
senses.example: The two accounts disagree on the time of the call.
senses.exampleCN: 两份记录对通话时间的说法不一致。
senses.why: When two records part company, at least one of them is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 两份记录一旦分道，至少有一份是错的。

senses.title: To upset the body
senses.definition: to make a person feel unwell, said of food or weather
senses.definitionCN: 指食物或气候让人身体不舒服
senses.example: Rich food disagrees with my stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 油腻的食物让我的胃不舒服。
senses.why: The body argues with what it cannot accept.
senses.whyCN: 身体接受不了的东西，它会自己争辩。

intro.en: Disagree is the negative prefix dis- added to agree, a verb English took from Old French agreer.
intro.cn: disagree 是否定前缀 dis- 加 agree，而 agree 来自古法语 agreer。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing or welcome.
items.cn: gratus 指令人愉快的、受欢迎的。

items.en: Agreer meant to please or to be to someone's liking.
items.cn: agreer 指使人高兴，或合某人的意。

items.en: Agree first meant to please, then to be of one mind.
items.cn: agree 先指使人满意，后指意见一致。

items.en: Disagree reversed that harmony into a clash of views.
items.cn: disagree 把这份和谐翻转成观点的冲撞。

items.en: The verb also covers records that do not match and food that upsets.
items.cn: 这个词也用于对不上的记录与让身体不适的食物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the agree stem, while the meaning group names different ways of standing against someone.
note.cn: 形近组共用 agree 这一段词干，近义组则区分几种与人相左的方式。

entries.definition: to have the same opinion as someone
entries.definitionCN: 与某人持相同看法

entries.definition: a state in which people hold different views
entries.definitionCN: 人们看法不同的状态

entries.definition: unpleasant or hard to get along with
entries.definitionCN: 令人不快或难以相处的

entries.definition: to be unlike, or to hold another view
entries.definitionCN: 不相同，或持另一种看法

entries.definition: to argue that something is not true
entries.definitionCN: 争辩某事不成立

entries.definition: to say that one is against something
entries.definitionCN: 表示反对某事

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from two heads shaking at a table to a stomach turning against rich food.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌边两个摇头的人，走到受不了油腻食物的胃。

normal.en: Dis- plus agree is agreement pulled apart.
normal.cn: dis- 加 agree，就是把一致拆开。

normal.en: Agree to disagree ends the argument without ending the friendship.
normal.cn: agree to disagree 结束了争论，却没结束交情。

normal.en: Two clocks that disagree cannot both be right.
normal.cn: 两只走时不一致的钟，不可能都对。

normal.en: When food disagrees with you, the stomach writes a protest.
normal.cn: 食物跟你不对付时，胃会写一封抗议信。

normal.en: To disagree is not to hate; it is only to see otherwise.
normal.cn: 不同意不等于厌恶，只是看到了别的样子。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pulling one sheet of paper in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手朝相反方向拉同一张纸。

abstract.en: Picture two clocks showing different hours on one wall.
abstract.cn: 想象同一面墙上两只钟指着不同的时间。

abstract.en: Picture a plate pushed away half finished.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘吃了一半就被推开的菜。

examples.en: I disagree with your first reason.
examples.cn: 我不同意你的第一个理由。

examples.en: The two reports disagree about the number of deaths.
examples.cn: 两份报告对死亡人数的说法不一致。

examples.en: They disagreed for an hour and then went home.
examples.cn: 他们争了一个小时，然后各自回家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disagree 记成「的士格瑞」：两个人为了打车费的哥争执起来，谁也不让谁。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 agree 构成。agree 来自古法语 agreer，源头是拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快的），本指合意、使人满意，后来才表示意见一致；加 dis- 之后，就表示看法不合、对不上，甚至让身体不适。

sensesIntro.en: From two minds that will not meet, to two records that will not match, to a body that refuses its food.
sensesIntro.cn: 从谈不拢的两个心思，到对不上的两份记录，再到拒绝食物的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pulling the same sheet of paper apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手把同一张纸往两边拉。

chain: TWO PEOPLE READ THE SAME PAGE

branches.en: The first sense is two minds that will not meet.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是两个谈不拢的心思。

branches.en: The second sense is two records that will not match.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是两份对不上的记录。

branches.en: The third sense is a body that refuses what it is given.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是拒绝所受之物的身体。

branches.en: People and papers both show the gap by failing to line up.
branches.cn: 人和纸都靠对不齐来显出那道缝。

branches.en: A clash of views and a clash in the stomach both end in discomfort.
branches.cn: 看法相撞与胃里相撞，最后都不舒服。

intro.en: Disagree gathers the agree family, words about harmony, consent and its opposite.
intro.cn: disagree 聚起 agree 一族词，围绕和睦、同意与相反面。

latinIntro.en: Latin gratus, pleasing, passed through Old French agreer and gave the base agree.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快）经古法语 agreer 传下，给出词基 agree。

items.example: They disagree about the cause of the fire.
items.exampleCN: 他们对起火原因意见不一。

items.example: We agree on the main point.
items.exampleCN: 我们在要点上看法一致。

items.meaning: a state of shared opinion or a formal deal
items.example: The two sides signed an agreement.
items.exampleCN: 双方签了一份协议。

items.example: A small disagreement grew into a quarrel.
items.exampleCN: 一点小分歧变成了争吵。

items.example: He can be a disagreeable guest.
items.exampleCN: 他有时是个让人不舒服的客人。

items.example: She gave an agreeable answer.
items.exampleCN: 她给了一个让人舒服的回答。

items.example: They met at the agreed place.
items.exampleCN: 他们在商定的地点见了面。

items.example: The room smelled disagreeably of smoke.
items.exampleCN: 屋里有一股难闻的烟味。

definition_en: a situation in which people have different opinions, or a failure of two things to match
core_image: 桌子两边各放一摞文件，中间空出一道谁也不过界的缝
scene: 两个人把各自的稿子拉回面前，谁也没有先开口。There was a sharp disagreement over the budget.
sceneCN: 这里 disagreement 指「分歧」（第 1 个义项：意见不合）；句意是双方在预算上分歧很大。

collocations.phrase: a disagreement between the two sides

senses.title: A clash of opinions
senses.definition: a state in which people hold different views about something
senses.definitionCN: 人们对某事的看法不一样的状态
senses.example: There was a sharp disagreement over the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在预算上分歧很大。
senses.why: Two certainties can stand face to face and both feel right.
senses.whyCN: 两个笃定可以面对面站着，各自都觉得对。

senses.title: An argument that follows
senses.definition: an angry exchange that grows out of different views
senses.definitionCN: 由看法不同发展成的激烈争执
senses.example: A small disagreement grew into a long quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 一点小分歧变成了一场长吵。
senses.why: The gap between two views becomes a noise before it closes.
senses.whyCN: 两种看法之间的缝，在合上之前先变成了声音。

senses.title: A failure to match
senses.definition: a difference between two things that should be the same
senses.definitionCN: 本应相同的两样东西之间出现的差异
senses.example: There is a disagreement between the two timetables.
senses.exampleCN: 两张时间表对不上。
senses.why: Two lists that should rhyme end on different sounds.
senses.whyCN: 两份本该押韵的清单，收在了不同的音上。

intro.en: Disagreement is disagreement in noun form: dis- plus agreement, which descends from Old French agreer.
intro.cn: disagreement 是动词 disagree 的名词形式：dis- 加 agreement，而 agreement 出自古法语 agreer。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing and welcome.
items.cn: gratus 指令人愉快、受欢迎的。

items.en: Agreer meant to please or to suit a person.
items.cn: agreer 指使人高兴或合某人的意。

items.en: Agreement named a state of being of one mind.
items.cn: agreement 指意见一致的状态。

items.en: Disagreement named the opposite state, and later a quarrel.
items.cn: disagreement 指相反的状态，后来又指争吵。

items.en: It also covers two records or figures that do not match.
items.cn: 它也可指两份记录或两个数字对不上。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on agree and its negation, while the meaning group names forms of conflict.
note.cn: 形近组建立在 agree 及其否定形式上，近义组则列出几种冲突。

entries.definition: a shared opinion or a formal arrangement
entries.definitionCN: 共同看法或正式约定

entries.definition: to hold a different opinion
entries.definitionCN: 持不同看法

entries.definition: unpleasant or hard to get along with
entries.definitionCN: 令人不快或难相处的

entries.definition: a serious argument about something important
entries.definitionCN: 围绕重要事情的严肃争论

entries.definition: a long struggle between opposing sides
entries.definitionCN: 对立双方之间的长期冲突

entries.definition: an angry talk in which people disagree
entries.definitionCN: 人们意见不合时的争吵

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a gap on a table to two sets of figures that will not agree.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌面上的一道缝，走到两组对不上的数字。

normal.en: Disagreement is the noun of the moment two views part.
normal.cn: disagreement 就是两种看法分开那一刻的名词。

normal.en: A sharp disagreement cuts the air before anyone raises a voice.
normal.cn: 尖锐的分歧，在有人提高嗓门之前就先划开了空气。

normal.en: Two timetables in disagreement cannot both be trusted.
normal.cn: 两张对不上的时间表，不能都信。

normal.en: Resolve the disagreement, and the table feels wider again.
normal.cn: 分歧一解开，桌子好像又宽了。

normal.en: The word keeps the gap visible without naming a winner.
normal.cn: 这个词让那道缝留在明处，却不判谁赢。

abstract.en: Picture two stacks of paper with a strip of bare wood between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两摞纸之间露出一条空木桌。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows pointing away from one point.
abstract.cn: 想象两个箭头从同一点朝外指去。

abstract.en: Picture two columns of figures that end on different totals.
abstract.cn: 想象两列数字收在不同的总数上。

examples.en: The disagreement was settled before lunch.
examples.cn: 分歧在午饭前就解决了。

examples.en: There is a serious disagreement between the two reports.
examples.cn: 两份报告之间存在严重的出入。

examples.en: They had a disagreement about who should pay.
examples.cn: 他们为该谁付钱发生了争执。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disagreement 记成「的士格瑞闷头」：两个人为了车费在的士里闷头争执，谁也不看谁。

root: 由 dis- 加 agreement 构成。agreement 出自古法语 agreer，源头是拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快的），本指合意与一致。加否定前缀后表示意见分开的状态，后来又引申为由此产生的争执，以及两份记录或数字之间的出入。

sensesIntro.en: From two views that will not meet, to the quarrel that follows, to two records that will not match.
sensesIntro.cn: 从谈不拢的两种看法，到随之而来的争吵，再到对不上的两份记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare strip of table between two stacks of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：两摞文件之间露出的那条空桌面。

chain: TWO PEOPLE SIT AT ONE TABLE
THE GAP IS NAMED AND FACED

branches.en: The first sense is the quiet fact of differing views.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是看法不同这件安静的事实。

branches.en: The second sense is the noise that grows out of it.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是由此长出来的声音。

branches.en: The third sense is the gap between things that should match.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是本该相同的两样东西之间的缝。

branches.en: A difference of view and an open quarrel share one root.
branches.cn: 看法不同与公开争吵共有一个根。

branches.en: People and papers both reveal a gap by failing to line up.
branches.cn: 人和纸都靠对不齐来显露那道缝。

intro.en: Disagreement sits in the agree family, beside agreement and disagree.
intro.cn: disagreement 处在 agree 一族里，与 agreement、disagree 相邻。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is gratus, pleasing, which reached English through Old French agreer.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁源头是 gratus（令人愉快），经古法语 agreer 进入英语。

items.example: The disagreement lasted all afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 分歧持续了一下午。

items.example: I disagree with that judgment.
items.exampleCN: 我不同意那个判断。

items.meaning: a shared opinion or a formal deal
items.example: They reached an agreement at last.
items.exampleCN: 他们终于达成了一致。

items.example: Both sides agree on the date.
items.exampleCN: 双方都同意这个日期。

items.example: The smell was disagreeable.
items.exampleCN: 那气味很难闻。

items.example: We spent an agreeable evening.
items.exampleCN: 我们度过了一个愉快的晚上。

items.example: They followed the agreed plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们照商定的方案办。

items.example: He spoke disagreeably to the waiter.
items.exampleCN: 他对服务员说话很难听。

definition_en: to stop being seen, or to stop existing
core_image: 魔术师把布一掀，桌上的鸟笼空了，只剩一根羽毛
scene: 灯忽然灭了，台上的人影没了，观众还以为这是节目的一部分。The coin seemed to disappear between his fingers.
sceneCN: 这里 disappear 指「消失」（第 1 个义项：看不见了）；句意是那枚硬币在他指间好像消失了。

senses.title: Out of sight
senses.definition: to pass out of sight so that the eye can no longer find it
senses.definitionCN: 离开视线，眼睛再也找不到
senses.example: The coin seemed to disappear between his fingers.
senses.exampleCN: 那枚硬币在他指间好像消失了。
senses.why: What the eye cannot follow, the mind cannot keep.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛跟不上的东西，脑子也留不住。

senses.title: Missing without explanation
senses.definition: to be lost or to go missing, often leaving no trace
senses.definitionCN: 走失或不见，往往不留痕迹
senses.example: Two hikers disappeared in the fog.
senses.exampleCN: 两名徒步者在雾里失踪了。
senses.why: The empty place asks a question that has no answer yet.
senses.whyCN: 那块空出来的地方，问出一个还没有答案的问题。

senses.title: Gone for good
senses.definition: to stop existing, as a species or a custom does
senses.definitionCN: 像物种或习俗那样不再存在
senses.example: Many old crafts are disappearing from the village.
senses.exampleCN: 村里许多老手艺正在消失。
senses.why: The last one goes, and nothing in the world can be asked again.
senses.whyCN: 最后一个没了，世上就再没有谁可以问了。

intro.en: Disappear is dis- added to appear, which comes from Latin apparere, to come into sight.
intro.cn: disappear 是 dis- 加 appear，而 appear 来自拉丁语 apparere（出现在眼前）。

items.en: Apparere meant to come into view or become visible.
items.cn: apparere 指进入视野或变得可见。

items.en: The prefix ad- added the sense of coming toward a place.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 添上「朝某处而来」的意思。

items.en: Appear entered English meaning to come in sight.
items.cn: appear 进入英语，意为出现在眼前。

items.en: Disappear reversed it into going out of sight.
items.cn: disappear 把它反过来，表示离开视线。

items.en: The word widened to missing people and vanishing species.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到失踪的人与消失的物种。

note.en: The look-alike group plays with appear and its forms, while the meaning group names ways of leaving no trace.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 appear 及其形式，近义组则列出几种不留痕迹的离开。

entries.definition: to come into sight
entries.definitionCN: 出现在视野中

entries.definition: the act of coming into sight, or the way something looks
entries.definitionCN: 出现这一动作，或某物的外表

entries.definition: easy to see or understand, or seeming true
entries.definitionCN: 显而易见的，或表面看来如此的

entries.definition: to disappear suddenly and completely
entries.definitionCN: 突然而彻底地消失

entries.definition: to grow weaker until it cannot be seen
entries.definitionCN: 渐渐变弱直到看不见

entries.definition: to turn into vapour and vanish from sight
entries.definitionCN: 化为蒸气而从眼前消失

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a coin hidden in a palm to a craft that leaves a village for good.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从藏在掌心的硬币，走到永远离开村庄的手艺。

normal.en: Dis- means away, so disappear is to take away the appearance.
normal.cn: dis- 是「离开」，disappear 就是把出现带走。

normal.en: The coin disappears because the hand closes.
normal.cn: 硬币之所以不见，是因为手掌合上了。

normal.en: A person disappears when no one can say where.
normal.cn: 一个人失踪，是没人说得出他在哪儿。

normal.en: A custom disappears when the last hand stops doing it.
normal.cn: 一门习俗消失，是最后一双手不再做了。

normal.en: What disappears leaves an outline where it used to be.
normal.cn: 消失的东西，会在原来的位置留下一个轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a palm opening over an empty table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌在空桌上摊开。

abstract.en: Picture fog closing over a path.
abstract.cn: 想象雾把小径合拢起来。

abstract.en: Picture a birdcage with the door open and no bird.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟笼门开着，里面没有鸟。

examples.en: The sun disappeared behind the hills.
examples.cn: 太阳落到山后不见了。

examples.en: Her bag disappeared from the table.
examples.cn: 她的包从桌上不见了。

examples.en: Whole species are disappearing as the forest shrinks.
examples.cn: 随着森林缩小，整个物种正在消失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disappear 记成「的士皮儿」：的士一开走，扬起的皮儿都散了，人影也没了。
